I have a clear picture:

1. **migrate-from.tsx** is an **Angular** component (not React). It has:
   - `useInterpolateSize` input (boolean, default false)
   - `isOpen` signal for toggling the AI response
   - Template with conditional classes and interpolate-size CSS
   - Scoped styles for `.interpolate-size`, `.message-container`, `.message-container.open`

2. **index.astro** uses `<app-chat-demo [useInterpolateSize]="false">` and `<app-chat-demo [useInterpolateSize]="true">` — Angular syntax. So the page currently expects Angular to be set up (or this might be copy-paste from another project and not actually working). Either way, we're migrating to Solid.

3. **Solid in this project**:
   - Components live in `src/components/solidjs/`
   - Import alias: `@/solid/` or `@/components/solidjs/` (both used)
   - Used in Astro with `client:only="solid-js"` for client-side rendering
   - Default export function components, props as function arguments

For the Solid migration:
- Convert Angular `input<boolean>(false)` → Solid props: `props: { useInterpolateSize?: boolean }` with default
- Convert `signal(false)` for isOpen → `createSignal(false)`
- Template: Angular `[class.x]="y"` → Solid `classList` or conditional `class={...}`; `(click)` → `onClick`; `{{ }}` → `{ }`
- Styles: Angular component styles → either a `<style>` block in the Solid component (if Astro/Solid supports it) or move to a scoped CSS module / global styles. In Solid (JSX), typically you use inline styles, Tailwind classes, or a separate CSS file. The component uses Tailwind for most things; the only custom CSS is:
  - `.interpolate-size { interpolate-size: allow-keywords; }`
  - `.message-container { height: 0; overflow: hidden; transition: ... }`
  - `.message-container.open { height: auto; }`
  So we need to keep those somewhere. Options: (1) Put them in the Astro page's `<style>` or a shared CSS file, (2) Use a Solid component with a `<style>` tag (works in Solid JSX), or (3) use inline styles where possible. The `interpolate-size` and `height: auto` are not doable with inline styles in a clean way, so we need a stylesheet. I'll plan to add a scoped style block in the Solid file or in the Astro page.

Checking Solid JSX: you can use `<style>` in Solid. So we can keep a `<style>` in the component with the same CSS.

Let me also confirm: in Solid, `class` is used for static classes, and `classList` for dynamic. So we'll have things like `class="border ..." classList={{ "interpolate-size": props.useInterpolateSize }}` and `classList={{ open: isOpen() }}`.

Creating the plan.

- **With interpolate-size:** “How can I smoothly animate to `height: auto` in modern CSS?”

- **Without interpolate-size:** Two paragraphs about the old limitation (no interpolation between fixed length and intrinsic keywords, so transitions to `height: auto` snap), plus the “The Old Way” code sample with the `/* Snaps! */` comment.

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
**Moving chat demo**

I'm moving ChatDemo to src/components/labs/ChatDemo.tsx. I'm extracting the MDX content into the ChatDemo component and deleting the old static page folder. 

**Adding layout support**

I'm adding layout support for labs, but will need to handle custom content structures separately. 

**Creating layout wrapper**

I'm creating a wrapper component that uses RootLayout with title and description from lab entry data and includes the style block. I'm adding the `interpolate-size` CSS property to the layout wrapper. 

**Passing chat demo**

I'm passing the ChatDemo component to Content for client:idle rendering. 

**Updating MDX integration**

I'm adding client:idle directive support for ChatDemo in MDX by using `<ChatDemo client:idle />` syntax. I'm adding title and description to the page head schema and considering layout options for labs. 

I'm implementing a single LabLayout for MDX content with RootLayout as the document wrapper. I'm adding the ChatDemo component to the MDX layout with inline styles. 

I'm rendering the MDX Content with ChatDemo component injected. I'm adding inline styles for chat demo animation transitions. </details></think>

{
  "markdown": "Content collections | Docs Skip to content\n\n# Content collections\n\nAdded in:&#96;astro@2.0.0&#96;\n\nContent collections are the best way to manage sets of content in any Astro project. Collections help to organize and query your documents, enable Intellisense and type checking in your editor, and provide automatic TypeScript type-safety for all of your content. Astro v5.0 introduced the Content Layer API for defining and querying content collections. This performant, scalable API provides built-in content loaders for your local collections. For remote content, you can use third-party and community-built loaders or create your own custom loader and pull in your data from any source.\n\n## What are Content Collections?\n\nYou can define a collection from a set of data that is structurally similar. This can be a directory of blog posts, a JSON file of product items, or any data that represents multiple items of the same shape.\n\nCollections stored locally in your project or on your filesystem can have entries of Markdown, MDX, Markdoc, YAML, TOML, or JSON files:\n\nsrc/\n\n- …\n\nnewsletter/ the “newsletter” collection\n\n- week-3.md a collection entry\n- week-2.md a collection entry\n- week-1.md a collection entry\n\nauthors/ the “author” collection\n\n- authors.json a single file containing all collection entries\n\nWith an appropriate collection loader, you can fetch remote data from any external source, such as a CMS, database, or headless payment system.\n\n## TypeScript configuration for collections\n\nContent collections rely on TypeScript to provide Zod validation, Intellisense and type checking in your editor. If you are not extending one of Astro’s&#96;strict&#96; or&#96;strictest&#96; TypeScript settings, you will need to ensure the following&#96;compilerOptions&#96; are set in your&#96;tsconfig.json&#96;:\n\ntsconfig.json\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n{  // Included with \"astro/tsconfigs/strict\" or \"astro/tsconfigs/strictest\"  \"extends\": \"astro/tsconfigs/base\",  \"compilerOptions\": {    \"strictNullChecks\": true, // add if using &#96;base&#96; template    \"allowJs\": true // required, and included with all Astro templates  }}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Defining Collections\n\nIndividual collections use&#96;defineCollection()&#96; to configure:\n\n- a&#96;schema&#96; for type safety (optional, but highly recommended!)\n- a&#96;loader&#96; for a data source (required)\n\n### The collection config file\n\nTo define collections, you must create a&#96;src/content.config.ts&#96; file in your project (&#96;.js&#96; and&#96;.mjs&#96; extensions are also supported.) This is a special file that Astro will use to configure your content collections based on the following structure:\n\nsrc/content.config.ts\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// 1. Import utilities from &#96;astro:content&#96;import { defineCollection } from 'astro:content';// 2. Import loader(s)import { glob, file } from 'astro/loaders';// 3. Import Zodimport { z } from 'astro/zod';// 4. Define your collection(s)const blog = defineCollection({ /* ... */ });const dogs = defineCollection({ /* ... */ });// 5. Export a single &#96;collections&#96; object to register your collection(s)export const collections = { blog, dogs };\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Defining the collection loader\n\nThe Content Layer API allows you to fetch your content (whether stored locally in your project or remotely) and uses a&#96;loader&#96; property to retrieve your data.\n\n#### Built-in loaders\n\nAstro provides [two built-in loader functions](https://docs.astro.build/en/reference/content-loader-reference/#built-in-loaders)(&#96;glob()&#96; and&#96;file()&#96;) for fetching your local content, as well as access to the API to construct your own loader and fetch remote data.\n\nThe [glob() loader](https://docs.astro.build/en/reference/content-loader-reference/#glob-loader) creates entries from directories of Markdown, MDX, Markdoc, JSON, YAML, or TOML files from anywhere on the filesystem. It accepts a&#96;pattern&#96; of entry files to match using glob patterns supported by [micromatch](https://github.com/micromatch/micromatch#matching-features), and a base file path of where your files are located. Each entry’s&#96;id&#96; will be automatically generated from its file name. Use this loader when you have one file per entry.\n\nThe [file() loader](https://docs.astro.build/en/reference/content-loader-reference/#file-loader) creates multiple entries from a single local file. Each entry in the file must have a unique&#96;id&#96; key property. It accepts a&#96;base&#96; file path to your file and optionally a&#96;parser&#96; function for data files it cannot parse automatically, or to parse data asynchronously. Use this loader when your data file can be parsed as an array of objects.\n\nsrc/content.config.ts\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nimport { defineCollection } from 'astro:content';import { glob, file } from 'astro/loaders'; // Not available with legacy APIimport { z } from 'astro/zod';const blog = defineCollection({  loader: glob({ pattern: \"**/*.md\", base: \"./src/data/blog\" }),  schema: /* ... */});const dogs = defineCollection({  loader: file(\"src/data/dogs.json\"),  schema: /* ... */});const probes = defineCollection({  // &#96;loader&#96; can accept an array of multiple patterns as well as string patterns  // Load all markdown files in the space-probes directory, except for those that start with \"voyager-\"  loader: glob({ pattern: ['*.md', '!voyager-*'], base: 'src/data/space-probes' }),  schema: z.object({    name: z.string(),    type: z.enum(['Space Probe', 'Mars Rover', 'Comet Lander']),    launch_date: z.date(),    status: z.enum(['Active', 'Inactive', 'Decommissioned']),    destination: z.string(),    operator: z.string(),    notable_discoveries: z.array(z.string()),  }),});export const collections = { blog, dogs, probes };\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n##### parser function\n\nThe&#96;file()&#96; loader accepts a second argument that defines a&#96;parser&#96; function. This allows you to specify a custom parser (e.g.&#96;csv-parse&#96;) to create a collection from a file’s contents.\n\nThe&#96;file()&#96; loader will automatically detect and parse (based on their file extension) a single array of objects from JSON and YAML files, and will treat each top-level table as an independent entry in TOML files. Support for these file types is built-in, and there is no need for a&#96;parser&#96; unless you have a nested JSON document. To use other files, such as&#96;.csv&#96;, you will need to create a parser function.\n\nThe following example shows importing a CSV parser, then loading a&#96;cats&#96; collection into your project by passing both a file path and&#96;parser&#96; function to the&#96;file()&#96; loader:\n\nsrc/content.config.ts\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nimport { defineCollection } from \"astro:content\";import { file } from \"astro/loaders\";import { parse as parseCsv } from \"csv-parse/sync\";const cats = defineCollection({  loader: file(\"src/data/cats.csv\", { parser: (text) = parseCsv(text, { columns: true, skipEmptyLines: true })})});\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nparseCsv(text, { columns: true, skipEmptyLines: true })})});\"\n\n###### Nested .json documents\n\nThe&#96;parser&#96; argument also allows you to load a single collection from a nested JSON document. For example, this JSON file contains multiple collections:\n\nsrc/data/pets.json\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n{\"dogs\": [{}], \"cats\": [{}]}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nYou can separate these collections by passing a custom&#96;parser&#96; to the&#96;file()&#96; loader for each collection:\n\nsrc/content.config.ts\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nconst dogs = defineCollection({  loader: file(\"src/data/pets.json\", { parser: (text) = JSON.parse(text).dogs })});const cats = defineCollection({  loader: file(\"src/data/pets.json\", { parser: (text) = JSON.parse(text).cats })});\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nJSON.parse(text).dogs })});const cats = defineCollection({ loader: file(\"src/data/pets.json\", { parser: (text) = JSON.parse(text).cats })});\"\n\n#### Building a custom loader\n\nYou can build a custom loader to fetch remote content from any data source, such as a CMS, a database, or an API endpoint.\n\nUsing a loader to fetch your data will automatically create a collection from your remote data. This gives you all the benefits of local collections, such as collection-specific API helpers such as&#96;getCollection()&#96; and&#96;render()&#96; to query and display your data, as well as schema validation.\n\n##### Inline loaders\n\nYou can define a loader inline, inside your collection, as an async function that returns an array of entries.\n\nThis is useful for loaders that don’t need to manually control how the data is loaded and stored. Whenever the loader is called, it will clear the store and reload all the entries.\n\nsrc/content.config.ts\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nconst countries = defineCollection({  loader: async () = {    const response = await fetch(\"https://restcountries.com/v3.1/all\");    const data = await response.json();    // Must return an array of entries with an id property, or an object with IDs as keys and entries as values    return data.map((country) = ({      id: country.cca3,      ...country,    }));  },  schema: /* ... */});\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n{ const response = await fetch(\"https://restcountries.com/v3.1/all\"); const data = await response.json(); // Must return an array of entries with an id property, or an object with IDs as keys and entries as values return data.map((country) = ({ id: country.cca3, ...country, })); }, schema: /* ... */});\"\n\nThe returned entries are stored in the collection and can be queried using the&#96;getCollection()&#96; and&#96;getEntry()&#96; functions.\n\n##### Loader objects\n\nFor more control over the loading process, you can use the Content Loader API to create a loader object. For example, with access to the&#96;load&#96; method directly, you can create a loader that allows entries to be updated incrementally or clears the store only when necessary.\n\nSimilar to creating an Astro integration or Vite plugin, you can [distribute your loader as an NPM package](https://docs.astro.build/en/reference/publish-to-npm/) that others can use in their projects.\n\nSee the full [Content Loader API](https://docs.astro.build/en/reference/content-loader-reference/) and examples of how to build your own loader.\n\n### Defining the collection schema\n\nSchemas enforce consistent frontmatter or entry data within a collection through Zod validation. A schema guarantees that this data exists in a predictable form when you need to reference or query it. If any file violates its collection schema, Astro will provide a helpful error to let you know.\n\nSchemas also power Astro’s automatic TypeScript typings for your content. When you define a schema for your collection, Astro will automatically generate and apply a TypeScript interface to it. The result is full TypeScript support when you query your collection, including property autocompletion and type-checking.\n\nEvery frontmatter or data property of your collection entries must be defined using a [Zod data type](https://docs.astro.build/en/reference/modules/astro-zod/#common-data-type-validators):\n\nsrc/content.config.ts\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nimport { defineCollection } from 'astro:content';import { glob, file } from 'astro/loaders';import { z } from 'astro/zod';const blog = defineCollection({  loader: glob({ pattern: \"**/*.md\", base: \"./src/data/blog\" }),  schema: z.object({    title: z.string(),    description: z.string(),    pubDate: z.coerce.date(),    updatedDate: z.coerce.date().optional(),  })});const dogs = defineCollection({  loader: file(\"src/data/dogs.json\"),  schema: z.object({    id: z.string(),    breed: z.string(),    temperament: z.array(z.string()),  }),});export const collections = { blog, dogs };\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### Defining datatypes with Zod\n\nAstro uses [Zod](https://github.com/colinhacks/zod) to power its content schemas. With Zod, Astro is able to validate every file’s data within a collection and provide automatic TypeScript types when you go to query content from inside your project.\n\nTo use Zod in Astro, import the&#96;z&#96; utility from&#96;\"astro/zod\"&#96;. This is a re-export of the Zod library, and it supports all of the features of Zod.\n\nSee the [z utility reference](https://docs.astro.build/en/reference/modules/astro-zod/) for a cheatsheet of common datatypes and to learn how Zod works and what features are available.\n\n##### Zod schema methods\n\nAll [Zod schema methods](https://docs.astro.build/en/reference/modules/astro-zod/#using-zod-methods)(e.g.&#96;.parse()&#96;,&#96;.transform()&#96;) are available, with some limitations. Notably, performing custom validation checks on images using&#96;image().refine()&#96; is unsupported.\n\n#### Defining collection references\n\nCollection entries can also “reference” other related entries.\n\nWith the [reference() function](https://docs.astro.build/en/reference/modules/astro-content/#reference) from the Collections API, you can define a property in a collection schema as an entry from another collection. For example, you can require that every&#96;space-shuttle&#96; entry includes a&#96;pilot&#96; property which uses the&#96;pilot&#96; collection’s own schema for type checking, autocomplete, and validation.\n\nA common example is a blog post that references reusable author profiles stored as JSON, or related post URLs stored in the same collection:\n\nsrc/content.config.ts\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nimport { defineCollection, reference } from 'astro:content';import { glob } from 'astro/loaders';import { z } from 'astro/zod';const blog = defineCollection({  loader: glob({ pattern: '**/[^_]*.md', base: \"./src/data/blog\" }),  schema: z.object({    title: z.string(),    // Reference a single author from the &#96;authors&#96; collection by &#96;id&#96;    author: reference('authors'),    // Reference an array of related posts from the &#96;blog&#96; collection by &#96;slug&#96;    relatedPosts: z.array(reference('blog')),  })});const authors = defineCollection({  loader: glob({ pattern: '**/[^_]*.json', base: \"./src/data/authors\" }),  schema: z.object({    name: z.string(),    portfolio: z.string().url(),  })});export const collections = { blog, authors };\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThis example blog post specifies the&#96;id&#96; s of related posts and the&#96;id&#96; of the post author:\n\nsrc/data/blog/welcome.md\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n---title: \"Welcome to my blog\"author: ben-holmes # references &#96;src/data/authors/ben-holmes.json&#96;relatedPosts:- about-me # references &#96;src/data/blog/about-me.md&#96;- my-year-in-review # references &#96;src/data/blog/my-year-in-review.md&#96;---\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThese references will be transformed into objects containing a&#96;collection&#96; key and an&#96;id&#96; key, allowing you to easily [query them in your templates](https://docs.astro.build/en/guides/content-collections/#accessing-referenced-data).\n\n### Defining custom IDs\n\nWhen using the&#96;glob()&#96; loader with Markdown, MDX, Markdoc, or JSON files, every content entry [id](https://docs.astro.build/en/reference/modules/astro-content/#id) is automatically generated in an URL-friendly format based on the content filename. The&#96;id&#96; is used to query the entry directly from your collection. It is also useful when creating new pages and URLs from your content.\n\nYou can override an entry’s generated&#96;id&#96; by adding your own&#96;slug&#96; property to the file frontmatter or data object for JSON files. This is similar to the “permalink” feature of other web frameworks.\n\nsrc/blog/1.md\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n---title: My Blog Postslug: my-custom-id/supports/slashes---Your blog post content here.\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nsrc/categories/1.json\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n{  \"title\": \"My Category\",  \"slug\": \"my-custom-id/supports/slashes\",  \"description\": \"Your category description here.\"}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Querying Collections\n\nAstro provides helper functions to query a collection and return one (or more) content entries.\n\n- [getEntry()](https://docs.astro.build/en/reference/modules/astro-content/#getentry) fetches a single entry from a collection.\n- [getCollection()](https://docs.astro.build/en/reference/modules/astro-content/#getcollection) fetches an entire collection and returns an array of entries.\n\nThese return entries with a unique&#96;id&#96;, a&#96;data&#96; object with all defined properties, and will also return a&#96;body&#96; containing the raw, uncompiled body of a Markdown, MDX, or Markdoc document.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nimport { getCollection, getEntry } from 'astro:content';// Get all entries from a collection.// Requires the name of the collection as an argument.const allBlogPosts = await getCollection('blog');// Get a single entry from a collection.// Requires the name of the collection and &#96;id&#96;const poodleData = await getEntry('dogs', 'poodle');\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThe sort order of generated collections is non-deterministic and platform-dependent. This means that if you are calling&#96;getCollection()&#96; and need your entries returned in a specific order (e.g. blog posts sorted by date), you must sort the collection entries yourself:\n\nsrc/pages/blog.astro\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n---import { getCollection } from 'astro:content';const posts = (await getCollection('blog')).sort(  (a, b) = b.data.pubDate.valueOf() - a.data.pubDate.valueOf(),);---\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nb.data.pubDate.valueOf() - a.data.pubDate.valueOf(),);---\"\n\nSee the full list of properties returned by the [CollectionEntry type](https://docs.astro.build/en/reference/modules/astro-content/#collectionentry).\n\n### Using content in Astro templates\n\nAfter querying your collections, you can access each entry’s content directly inside of your Astro component template. For example, you can create a list of links to your blog posts, displaying information from your entry’s frontmatter using the&#96;data&#96; property.\n\nsrc/pages/index.astro\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n---import { getCollection } from 'astro:content';const posts = await getCollection('blog');---\u003ch1My posts\u003c/h1\u003cul  {posts.map(post = (    \u003cli\u003ca href={&#96;/blog/${post.id}&#96;}{post.data.title}\u003c/a\u003c/li  ))}\u003c/ul\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nMy posts {posts.map(post = ( {post.data.title} ))}\"\n\n#### Rendering body content\n\nOnce queried, you can render Markdown and MDX entries to HTML using the [render()](https://docs.astro.build/en/reference/modules/astro-content/#render) function property. Calling this function gives you access to rendered HTML content, including both a&#96; &#96;&#96;&#96;\n---import { getEntry, render } from 'astro:content';const entry = await getEntry('blog', 'post-1');if (!entry) {  // Handle Error, for example:  throw new Error('Could not find blog post 1');}const { Content, headings } = await render(entry);---\u003cpPublished on: {entry.data.published.toDateString()}\u003c/p\u003cContent /\n&#96;&#96;&#96;&#96;&#96;&#96;\n---import type { CollectionEntry } from 'astro:content';interface Props {  post: CollectionEntry\u003c'blog';}// &#96;post&#96; will match your 'blog' collection schema typeconst { post } = Astro.props;---\n&#96;&#96;&#96;&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Example: Filter out content entries with &#96;draft: true&#96;import { getCollection } from 'astro:content';const publishedBlogEntries = await getCollection('blog', ({ data }) = {  return data.draft !== true;});\n&#96;&#96;&#96;&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Example: Filter out content entries with &#96;draft: true&#96; only when building for productionimport { getCollection } from 'astro:content';const blogEntries = await getCollection('blog', ({ data }) = {  return import.meta.env.PROD ? data.draft !== true : true;});\n&#96;&#96;&#96;&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// Example: Filter entries by sub-directory in the collectionimport { getCollection } from 'astro:content';const englishDocsEntries = await getCollection('docs', ({ id }) = {  return id.startsWith('en/');});\n&#96;&#96;&#96;&#96;&#96;&#96;\n---import { getEntry, getEntries } from 'astro:content';const blogPost = await getEntry('blog', 'welcome');// Resolve a singular reference (e.g. &#96;{collection: \"authors\", id: \"ben-holmes\"}&#96;)const author = await getEntry(blogPost.data.author);// Resolve an array of references// (e.g. &#96;[{collection: \"blog\", id: \"about-me\"}, {collection: \"blog\", id: \"my-year-in-review\"}]&#96;)const relatedPosts = await getEntries(blogPost.data.relatedPosts);---\u003ch1{blogPost.data.title}\u003c/h1\u003cpAuthor: {author.data.name}\u003c/p\u003c!-- ... --\u003ch2You might also like:\u003c/h2{relatedPosts.map(post = (  \u003ca href={post.id}{post.data.title}\u003c/a))}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;&#96;&#96;&#96;\n---import { getCollection, render } from 'astro:content';// 1. For your template, you can get the entry directly from the propconst { post } = Astro.props;const { Content } = await render(post);---\u003ch1{post.data.title}\u003c/h1\u003cContent /\n&#96;&#96;&#96;&#96;&#96;&#96;\n---import { getEntry, render } from \"astro:content\";// 1.
